I think there is a distinction to be made as well. There are lotto players and then there are lotto players. Someone who invests hundreds of dollars weekly into these games is an idiot. I've known several people who have done this their entire lives, and they'll celebrate when once every 5 or 6 years they win $5,000 or $10,000, not stopping to think how much they lost to win that sum. Yet, there are others, who know their lot in life, tend to live on a ostensibly good budget, and just for fun will play one or two tickets per week and spend less than $5.

There is a difference here. The latter knows that their odds are stupendously low. But they do it for the romance, and they sacrifice only a few bucks to do it. Just for the dream, because in the existential tragedy that is life, hope and pipe dreams are just a little glimmer of sunlight on what have otherwise been a shitty day at work. The kind of hope they display here is the existential kind, and not altogether different than the hope we have of life after death, or there being some meaning to everything. It's that there might be a higher order to life, and maybe that order will poke through the iron curtain today. On this ticket. Maybe the numbers will work out today. Maybe.

That maybe is really just a referent that stands for something to look forward to. It doesn't mean that this is all they are looking forward to. Perhaps they are rationally and studiously putting funds into retirement accounts and preparing in the sort of sterile way, the "accounting" way. But those kinds of things don't tend to fulfill a need we have to believe that there is some "magic" in life. A few bucks a week to believe in that kind of far flung possibility might be worth it.
